note: Static explainers for Macro Engine pillars, keyed by engine row id. Content: Hercules (COLLAB.md spec, 2026-10-08). Update `live` as conditions change.

fiscal.body: Deficits, debt sustainability, sovereign spreads. Funds stress leaks into the currency.
fiscal.live: CORRECTION (Oct 21): no US shutdown — Trump signed the CR Sept 2, funded through Dec 11; Sept jobs/CPI/PPI/housing all printed on schedule (the 'shutdown day 20' line was bad data). France: Moody's reviews France Friday (Aa3 negative → cut to A1 widely expected); OAT 10Y 5.00%; OAT-Bund ~157-160bp; revenue-section first reading Oct 27 (49.3 floated); Nov-5 cross-sector strike called. UK: Sep borrowing £24.5B miss (vs £23.9B), debt >£3T first time; Healey's first Budget Oct 28.
fiscal.title: Fiscal & sovereign risk

growth.body: Who is accelerating, who is stalling (GDP, jobs, PMIs). Always comparative. Stronger growth pulls in capital and raises hike expectations.
growth.live: US: jobless claims BEAT 194K (vs 200K fcst; near 57-year lows) — low-hire, low-fire intact; housing soft patch (starts 1.221M miss, pending home sales -7.3% record low, ADP 18.5K) vs last week's retail/IP beats; leading index flat beat (0.0% vs -0.2%). UK: jobs beat (unemp 4.7%) + GDP +0.1% beat vs CBI orders -32 miss. China: Q3 GDP 4.5% beat; FDI decline narrowing (-4.3% y/y Jan-Sep). Australia: employment -39.3K, unemp 4.7% five-year high. Canada: IPPI +2.0% beat, RMPI +4.8% beat today.
growth.title: Growth differentials

inflation.body: CPI/PCE vs the central bank's target. High inflation alone strengthens nothing — what matters is what the bank does about it.
inflation.live: US CPI 3.7%, PPI hot; import prices +8.1% y/y (4-yr high); crude surging (Brent $113.20 +4%, WTI $99.45 +2.4% on NYT Iran-strike plans) — energy re-acceleration risk. UK Sep CPI verified 3.5% y/y beat (vs 3.4% fcst; highest since Oct 2025 on energy; core 2.8% in line; services 3.7% sticky) — locks the Nov-5 BoE hike. German Sep PPI +6.7% y/y beat (vs 6.2%). NZ Q3 CPI soft miss: 0.7% q/q, 3.7% y/y (vs 0.8%/3.8%; below RBNZ's 3.9% proj, still above 1-3% target) — hike stayed ~98% priced. Japan national core CPI tonight 18:30 CT (2.1% fcst).
inflation.title: Inflation

policy.body: Central banks moving in different directions. It is the gap between them that moves currencies: money flows toward higher rates.
policy.live: Oct 27-28 FOMC a hold at ~89% (fed funds futures, Ausecure Oct 22 — ~11% hike odds, down from ~13%); December hike ~90% (CME FedWatch). BoC Oct 28 hike ~93-95% (CORRA OIS); RBNZ Oct 28 hike ~98% (Reuters Oct 22) — the soft NZ CPI didn't dent it. ECB Oct 29 hold virtually certain; Dec hike ~88%. BoE Nov 5 hike ~98.8%. BoJ Oct 29-30 hold ~95%+; Dec hike ~73-74%. RBA Nov 2-3 hike ~42% (Goldman flipped to a Nov call).
policy.title: Policy divergence

positioning.body: Where speculators already stand (CFTC COT, Fridays). Crowded trades are fragile: if everyone is long dollars, nobody is left to buy. The contrarian lens — where would a surprise hurt most.
positioning.live: New CFTC (Oct 13 report): all G10 signals neutral (0). Splits: hedge funds flipped AGAINST the yen while real money bets FOR it; hedge funds for the Aussie but real money strongly against. Funds strongly short CAD (added sharply). No crowded-long unwind risk anywhere — the pain trade is two-sided.
positioning.title: Positioning

risk.body: Risk-on vs risk-off. Fear bids USD, JPY, CHF (havens) and sells AUD, NZD, GBP (risk proxies).
risk.live: Risk-off: Nasdaq/S&P plunged on AI-spending concerns (Lam Research -10%, Meta down post-earnings); 10Y sank below 5% (-18bp) as investors fled to bonds; DXY 101.62 near the 3-week low — no USD haven bid even on the Gulf escalation (NYT: US/Israel drew up specific Iran-strike plans for after Nov-3 midterms; US ordered diplomats out of Saudi Arabia; Houthi attacks). Haven bid went to the yen (USD/JPY -0.8%, best day in a month), not the dollar or franc.
risk.title: Risk sentiment

tot.body: Export prices vs import prices: oil, metals. The same price moves two currencies opposite ways — say which and why.
tot.live: Brent $113.20 (+4%, near 5-month high) and WTI $99.45 (+2.4%) on the NYT Iran-strike plans + Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia; Brent-WTI spread ~$13.75 — the geopolitical-premium gauge. Gold $4,045 (-2.5%, 5th straight down day) despite falling yields — selling with stocks, not on rates. Canada upstream heat: IPPI +2.0% m/m (+14.5% y/y), RMPI +4.8% m/m (+27.0% y/y). GDT powders firm (WMP +4.4%, SMP +3.4%).
tot.title: Terms of trade
